name: pmxt
what_it_holds: "CCXT for prediction markets": a unified Python/TypeScript SDK, hosted API, self-hostable server, CLI, and MCP integration that normalizes access across Polymarket, Polymarket US, Kalshi, Limitless, Probable, Baozi, Myriad, Opinion, Metaculus, Smarkets, Hyperliquid, Gemini Titan, SuiBets, Rain, and Hunch. MIT licensed, 2.1k stars/269 forks, 1,687 commits, actively developed.
why_useful: One client library to pull current AND (via each venue's own history endpoints) historical market data across a dozen-plus prediction-market venues including Metaculus, rather than writing bespoke API clients per platform — useful if the team wants to pull ABNB-earnings or travel/regulation contracts across multiple venues with one interface.
time_coverage: N/A (live API wrapper; historical depth depends on underlying venue APIs)
last_activity: 1,687 commits, actively maintained as of fetch
themes: Prediction markets and betting data: Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold APIs and datasets on earnings and travel/regulation events
why_all: One client library to pull current AND (via each venue's own history endpoints) historical market data across a dozen-plus prediction-market venues including Metaculus, rather than writing bespoke API clients per platform — useful if the team wants to pull ABNB-earnings or travel/regulation contracts across multiple venues with one interface.

name: safegraph_py
what_it_holds: Official SafeGraph Python library (203 commits) for wrangling SafeGraph 'Patterns' (weekly/monthly visit-frequency), 'Core' (place/POI reference), 'Geo' and 'Social Distancing' mobility files, plus 2016-2019 Census/CBG demographic joins. No data files committed -- it is a client for SafeGraph's (largely paywalled now, some free/academic tiers) place-visit data. Foot-traffic-by-POI is a plausible STR/hospitality demand proxy (hotel/lodging POIs, restaurant/attraction visits near lodging markets) if any free tier or academic snapshot is still reachable.
why_useful: If the team ever obtains SafeGraph/Advan/Dewey foot-traffic samples (e.g. via academic access), this is the standard toolkit to normalize POI-level visit counts into a usable travel/leisure foot-traffic index (hotels, tourist attractions, airports) as an ABNB demand proxy.
geography: US-centric POI categories (SafeGraph's core panel), extensible
themes: Public-health and mobility indices: Google/Apple mobility archives, Cuebiq, SafeGraph/Advan/Dewey samples, Placer.ai-like foot traffic, mobility datasets by city
Alternative-data vendor sample repos: vendors publishing free samples on GitHub (Advan, Similarweb, Apptopia, Yipit-like, Consumer Edge, Earnest, M Science, Quiver Quant, Thinknum)
why_all: If the team ever obtains SafeGraph/Advan/Dewey foot-traffic samples (e.g. via academic access), this is the standard toolkit to normalize POI-level visit counts into a usable travel/leisure foot-traffic index (hotels, tourist attractions, airports) as an ABNB demand proxy.

Addresses gap #6 (consumer/foot-traffic panels) and gap #8 (hotel/lodging demand proxies) if a free SafeGraph sample or academic dataset can still be pulled; also a template for point-of-interest visit-pattern ingestion generally.

name: OSMPythonTools
what_it_holds: Python library (GPL-3.0, 487 stars, 177 commits) wrapping the Overpass API, Nominatim, and OSM API. Supports tag-based queries (e.g. `tourism=hotel`), reverse geocoding, GeoJSON export, and can track how a specific OSM object's tags changed over time (useful for a rough time series on individual hotel/venue records, though not scalable to full-city historical censuses since Overpass itself has no full history by default).
why_useful: Lower-effort alternative to pyrosm for smaller, per-city, live Overpass pulls of tourism=hotel/guest_house/apartment POIs when a full Geofabrik PBF isn't needed; the per-object history feature is a rare free way to see an individual venue's tag history.
last_activity: Maintained (noted activity 2017-2022 window in fetch, likely with intermittent updates since)
themes: POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps

name: OSMnx
what_it_holds: Widely used Python package for downloading/modeling/analyzing OSM street networks, building footprints, transit, and 'urban amenities/points of interest' by place name or polygon.
why_useful: General-purpose alternative for pulling POI/amenity layers (including tourism/lodging tags) by named city or custom polygon, complementing pyrosm for smaller ad hoc pulls.
